We need SMILES of the whole molecule given fragments: 'CC(=O)O' (acetate? actually acetic acid) and 'Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O' (p-hydroxybenzoic acid? Wait: Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O is salicylic acid? Let's parse: phenyl with OH at position 1 (attached to O) and COOH at position? The SMILES: O c1 c c c c c1 C(=O)O. That is phenol with carboxylic acid para? Actually the O attached to aromatic carbon is phenoxy? The SMILES starts with O attached to aromatic carbon: O-Ph-COOH. That's hydroxybenzoic acid? The OH is attached to aromatic carbon (phenol). So it's hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid is ortho OH and COOH). The SMILES given is "Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O" which is para? Not specified; default is OH at position 1, COOH at position 1? Actually the ring numbering: c1ccccc1 is benzene; preceding O attaches to first carbon (position 1). Then after the ring, C(=O)O attaches to the same carbon? Wait SMILES: Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O means O attached to aromatic carbon (position 1) and after the ring closure, C(=O)O attached to the same carbon (position 1) as a substituent? That would be a phenol with carboxylic acid at same carbon, which is impossible (two substituents on same carbon). Actually SMILES reading: O c1 c c c c c1 C(=O)O. The O is attached to the aromatic carbon at start of ring (c1). Then after the ring closure, the carbon after the ring (C(=O)O) is attached to the aromatic carbon that closed the ring (the same carbon as the O?). In SMILES, you can have two substituents on same aromatic carbon by writing "Oc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)O". The given "Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O" is ambiguous but likely means phenol with COOH at para? Actually typical SMILES for salicylic acid is "O=C(O)c1ccccc1O". For p-hydroxybenzoic acid: "O=C(O)c1ccc(cc1)O". The given is reversed order but similar.

Now we also have fragment "CC(=O)O" which is acetic acid (CH3COOH). The whole molecule formula C9H8O4. Let's compute: C9 H8 O4. That's aspirin? Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) formula C9H8O4 indeed. Yes aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid: has an acetyl group attached to phenoxy of salicylic acid (i.e., O-acetyl). The fragments: CC(=O)O is acetyl group (acetate) but actually acetyl group is CH3CO- attached via O to phenyl. The other fragment is phenyl with OH and COOH (salicylic acid). Combined yields aspirin: O-acetylsalicylic acid: SMILES "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O". Let's verify: aspirin SMILES is "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O". Yes.

Thus answer is that SMILES.

We should maybe validate with tool but not needed. Could quickly validate.
